title: PolicySetRuleParams
description: Params for policy.setRule: ONE invocation rule. The rule carries what it SAYS and nothing about where it came from — createdAt, source and evaluatorVersion are facts the store records about the write, not claims a caller may make, and a renderer that could set them could dress a rule it wrote as one a person answered.

id.description: The rule to REPLACE. Absent writes a new rule and the backend mints its id (AD-7); present must name a rule the document already carries, and an id naming nothing is invalid params. A renderer may replace a rule it can see, and may not choose the identity of a new one.

selector.description: WHICH invocations the rule speaks about, and nothing about what it decides: exactly one of the three is set. 'exact' names a fixed command line positionally; 'program' covers every argument list of one command word and may only permit while bound to the effect it was granted under; 'hasFeature' matches a semantic fact the CLASSIFIER recorded and may never permit. The asymmetry is enforced by content's own gate, not restated here.

exact.description: A fixed number of subcommands and a fixed number of tokens in each, matched positionally. A '*' in a token matches any contents of that one token and never spans a token boundary or a shell separator.

program.description: One command word, carrying ANY arguments.

hasFeature.description: One command word carrying one feature of the classifier's CLOSED vocabulary. Both halves are required: a feature alone would speak for every program that can carry it.

decision.description: What the rule decides for the invocations its selector covers.

grantedUnder.description: The effect class a widening permit was granted for, checked against the effect the CALL classified as. Absent on a rule that does not widen.
